result.title: AutoVend: Benchmarking LLM Agents on Long-Horizon Autonomous Vending Operations
result.summary: Large language model (LLM) agents are extending agent-mediated commerce on the Web from shopping for consumers to operating businesses for sellers. In online-to-offline (O2O) commerce, decisions are issued through Web-based platforms but realized through costly physical execution. Evaluating such agents requires going beyond individual transactions to ask whether decisions made online turn into sustained economic returns. We introduce AutoVend, a benchmark in which one LLM agent manages 20 vending machines across five site types through a Web-based operating interface for 180 simulated days. Its data-grounded simulator combines a shared warehouse, procurement lead times, paid replenishment, inventory expiration, and recurring operating costs. We evaluate five LLM agents against a rule-based inventory-control baseline and diagnose their site coordination, execution, and performance over time. Four of five evaluated LLM agents fall short of this baseline, and returns per dollar of inference cost rank models differently from returns alone. Operational analyses show that gains in individual metrics do not consistently yield stronger economic growth, as inventory and execution costs erode these gains. Trajectory analysis further reveals difficulties in grounding feasible actions, managing inventory commitments, and converting feedback into effective policy revisions.

AI.brief_summary: AutoVend 构建了一个长时程自主运营基准：单个 LLM agent 通过网页界面在 180 个模拟日内经营 20 台自动售货机，环境包含共享仓库、采购提前期、付费补货、库存过期与持续运营成本，作者将其与规则式库存控制基线对比，并对多个模型的执行轨迹与反馈利用进行分析。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「每美元推理成本对应回报」以及「反馈能否转化为有效策略修订」的评估视角，可能为 LVR 中动态计算与停止决策的收益-成本权衡提供参考，但该工作不含视觉输入或 latent 状态，联系较远，需较多核查。
